_raw_content.post_desc:
Namsan Seoul Tower, which has established itself as a romantic island in the heart of the city, is a 236.7-meter-tall tower located at the summit of Namsan Mountain (262m), a place long regarded as a site of good fortune for lifelong love. Offering a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic view of Seoul from an elevation of 480 meters above sea level, it boasts the best vantage point in the city. As a symbol of Seoul and the top tourist destination chosen by international visitors, it has become a romantic sanctuary for couples worldwide who dream of eternal love. Popular attractions for couples include the "Locks of Love" and "Heart Chair," which are widely appreciated.


Namsan Seoul Tower comprises two main sections: the Lower Seoul Tower Plaza and the Upper N Seoul Tower. The Seoul Tower Plaza spans from the 1st to the 4th floor and includes attractions such as Gallery K, the Bodyfriend Lounge, and the Game Plaza. Visitors can also enjoy media art installations on a large 55-inch OLED panel. From the 5th floor up to the T7 floor, the N Seoul Tower features observation decks, the N Gift Shop, and various restaurants and cafes, all open 365 days a year.


Frequently Asked Questions about Namsan Seoul Tower
Can I visit Namsan Seoul Tower on national holidays or regular holidays?
Yes. The Namsan Seoul Tower is open 365 days a year. (As of 2026)
Can I visit Namsan Seoul Tower with my pet?
Pets are not allowed at the Namsan Seoul Tower. (As of 2026)
What are the operating hours of the Namsan Seoul Tower Cable Car and how much is it?
Namsan Seoul Tower Cable Car operates from 10 am to 11 pm. The ticket prices are as follows. (As of 2026)

• Round-trip fare: Adults 15,000 KRW / Children 11,500 KRW
• One-way fare: Adults 12,000 KRW / Children 9,000 KRW
(Children: From 36 months to elementary school students)

_raw_content.post_desc:
都心のロマンチックアイランドとしてその地位を確立した「南山ソウルタワー」は、昔から夫婦円満のパワースポットとして広く知られ、ナムサン(南山:262m)の頂上に位置する、高さ236.7mのタワーです。海抜480mの地点からソウル市の360度パノラマビューを一望できる最高の展望を誇ります。外国人が選ぶ観光名所1位にも選ばれたことのあるソウルのシンボルであり、永遠の愛を夢見る世界中の恋人たちのロマンスの聖地でもあります。恋人たちのためのロマンチックな体験コンテンツ「愛の南京錠」と「ハートの椅子」が大人気です。 

南山ソウルタワーは、下層部の「ソウルタワープラザ」と上層部の「Nソウルタワー」で構成されています。1階から4階までは「ソウルタワープラザ」で、ギャラリーKやボディフレンド・ラウンジ、ゲームプラザなどがあり、55型の大型OLEDパネルでメディアアート作品を鑑賞することができます。5階から始まり、T1～T7階までは「Nソウルタワー」で、展望台やNギフトショップ、さまざまなレストランやカフェがあり、365日年中無休で利用することができます。

_raw_content.post_desc:
南山首尔塔作为首尔市中心的浪漫地标，稳固地占据了一席之地。它矗立于历史悠久、寓意着长久相伴的南山之巅，海拔高度达236.7米，加之南山本身的262米高度，使得游客能在总计约480米的高空，尽情享受首尔市的全景风光，视野无比开阔。作为首尔昔日外国游客心目中的旅游首选之地，南山首尔塔不仅是这座城市的象征，更是全球恋人们梦寐以求的浪漫殿堂，在这里，特别为情侣们设计的“爱情锁”和“心形椅子”等浪漫体验项目深受喜爱。 

南山首尔塔由下层首尔塔广场和上层N首尔塔组成。 1楼到4楼是首尔塔广场,有Gallery K和Body Friend Lounge、Game Plaza等,通过55型大型OLED面板可以欣赏到媒体艺术雕塑。 从5楼到T1~T7楼是N首尔塔，设有瞭望台、N礼品店、各种餐厅和咖啡厅，365天全年无休。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Gyeongbokgung Palace was the first and largest of the royal palaces built during the Joseon Dynasty. Built in 1395, Gyeongbokgung Palace was located at the heart of the newly appointed capital of Seoul (then known as Hanyang) and represented the sovereignty of the Joseon Dynasty. The largest of the Five Grand Palaces (the others being Gyeonghuigung Palace, Deoksugung Palace, Changgyeonggung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace), Gyeongbokgung served as the main palace of the Joseon Dynasty.


The Korean government has invested much time and effort into rebuilding, restoring, and maintaining the palace for future generations. These efforts include work to rebuild and restore the buildings that were destroyed during the Japanese occupation. Visitors to Gyeongbokgung can also visit the National Palace Museum of Korea and the National Folk Museum of Korea as they are located on the palace grounds.

 

To increase ease of accessibility from Gyeongbokgung Palace to Seochon and vice versa, the palace's western gate, Yeongchumun, was opened to the public on December 2018. For the past 43 years, there were only 3 entrances to Gyeongbokgung Palace - the southern gate Gwanghwamun, the northern gate Sinmumun, and the eastern entrance of National folk Museum of Korea. However, with the opening of the western gate Yeongchumun, entry to the palace from all directions has been now made possible.


Frequently Asked Questions about Gyeongbokgung Palace
When is Gyeongbokgung Palace closed?
Gyeongbokgung Palace is closed every Tuesday.
If a public holiday and a closed day overlap, the doors will be opened. As a result, the first non-holiday following the open holiday will be the closed day. (As of 2026)
Can I visit Gyeongbokgung Palace for free if I wear a hanbok?
Yes, you can. You can enter Gyeongbokgung Palace for free if you wear a complete hanbok.
Please refer to the guidelines regarding detailed hanbok regulations. (As of 2026)
How can I participate in the Gyeongbokgung Palace guided tour?
Groups of less than ten individuals can participate in the guided tour without reservation. Groups of 10 or more people need to make a reservation, and up to 30 people can participate in the tour. You can participate in the regular guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace without any reservations. During the tour, you'll hear the storyteller's narration as you explore the main pavilions of the palace. English tours are available daily at 11:00, 13:30, and 15:30 (except on Tuesdays.) (As of 2026)
Go to Gyeongbokgung Palace Management Office Guided Tour

_raw_content.post_desc:
キョンボックン(景福宮)は朝鮮王朝時代に建てられた王宮の中で最も大きい宮殿だった。朝鮮王朝開国3年の1395年に完工した宮殿は390数両で漢陽の中心軸に位置した。開国の功臣、チョン・ドジョン(鄭道伝)はテジョ(太祖)から最初の宮殿の名前を付けなさいという命を受けており、苦心の末に「新しい王朝が大きな幸運を享受して繁栄する」という意味でキョンボックン(景福宮)と名付けた。キョンボックン(景福宮)は5代の宮であるキョンヒグン(慶熙宮)、トクスグン(徳寿宮)、チャンギョングン(昌慶宮)、チャンドッグン(昌徳宮)の中で最も大きい宮殿で、朝鮮王朝の宮殿의役割をした。

国宝第223号のクンジョンジョン(勤政殿)はキョンボックン(景福宮)の法典に、各種の即位式を挙行した王室のイベント会場だった。クンジョンジョン(勤政殿)の横に位置したキョンфеル(慶会楼)は1万ウォンの旧貨幤掲載されるだけに、代表的な建築物として愛されてきた。韓国は未来世代を向けて宮殿の再建、復元、維持のために多くの時間と努力を投資してきた。それ以外にも日本統治時代に毀損を経験したが、2010年に完全に復元されたクァンファムン(光化門)、コジョン(高宗)とミョンソンファンフ(明成皇后)が泊まっていたコンチョングン(乾淸宮)、キョンボックン(景福宮)の後苑の香遠亭などが位置している。キョンボックン(景福宮)を訪問する際、国立古宮博物館や国立民俗博物館も一緒に訪問しやすい。

キョンボックン(景福宮)は朝鮮王朝最高の宮殿であるだけに思ったより広い。動線は自由に調整することができる。ただしもっと詳しいの観覧を希望すれば、我々宮殿管理人ガイドの説明と共にすることが一番いい。

キョンボックン(景福宮) {text-align: justify; } とソチョン(西村)エリアの観覧客の利便性を高め、経済活性化のために、キョンボックン(景福宮)の西門であるヨンチュムン(迎秋門)が2018年12月より全面的に開放されました。キョンボックン(景福宮)の出入り口は今まで南側のクァンファムン(光化門)、北側のシンムムン(神武門)、東側の韓国国立民俗博物館の出入り口など3つの門が開放されていましたが、43年ぶりにヨンチュムン(迎秋門)が開放されたことで、東・西・南・北全ての門で出入りが可能となりました。


キョンボックン(景福宮)についてよくある質問
キョンボックン(景福宮)の定休日はいつですか？
キョンボックン(景福宮)の休館日は毎週火曜日です。
ただし、祝日と休館日が重なる日は開館し、開館した日の次の最初の開館日を休みとします。(2026年基準)
韓服を着ればキョンボックン(景福宮)を無料で観覧できますか？
はい。韓服を着用した方は、キョンボックン(景福宮)の入場が無料です。
韓服についての詳しい規定はガイドラインを参照してください。
キョンボックン(景福宮)の解説ツアーにはどうやって参加できますか？

description: キョンボックン(景福宮)は朝鮮王朝時代に建てられた王宮の中で最も大きい宮殿だった。朝鮮王朝開国3年の1395年に完工した宮殿は390数両で漢陽の中心軸に位置した。開国の功臣、チョン・ドジョン(鄭道伝)はテジョ(太祖)から最初の宮殿の名前を付けなさいという命を受けており、苦心の末に「新しい王朝が大きな幸運を享受して繁栄する」という意味でキョンボックン(景福宮)と名付けた。キョンボックン(景福宮)は5代の宮であるキョンヒグン(慶熙宮)、トクスグン(徳寿宮)、チャンギョングン(昌慶宮)、チャンドッグン(昌徳宮)の中で最も大きい宮殿で、朝鮮王朝の宮殿의役割をした。 国宝第223号のクンジョンジョン(勤政殿)はキョンボックン(景福宮)の法典に、各種の即位式を挙行した王室のイベント会場だった。クンジョンジョン(勤政殿)の横に位置したキョンфеル(慶会楼)は1万ウォンの旧貨幤掲載されるだけに、代表的な建築物として愛されてきた。韓国は未来世代を向けて宮殿の再建、復元、維持のために多くの時間と努力を投資してきた。それ以外にも日本統治時代に毀損を経験したが、2010年に完全に復元されたクァンファムン(光化門)、コジョン(高宗)とミョンソンファンフ(明成皇后)が泊まっていたコンチョングン(乾淸宮)、キョンボックン(景福宮)の後苑の香遠亭などが位置している。キョンボックン(景福宮)を訪問する際、国立古宮博物館や国立民俗博物館も一緒に訪問しやすい。 キョンボックン(景福宮)は朝鮮王朝最高の宮殿であるだけに思ったより広い。動線は自由に調整することができる。ただしもっと詳しいの観覧を希望すれば、我々宮殿管理人ガイドの説明と共にすることが一番いい。 キョンボックン(景福宮) {text-align: justify; } とソチョン(西村)エリアの観覧客の利便性を高め、経済活性化のために、キョンボックン(景福宮)の西門であるヨンチュムン(迎秋門)が2018年12月より全面的に開放されました。キョンボックン(景福宮)の出入り口は今まで南側のクァンファムン(光化門)、北側のシンムムン(神武門)、東側の韓国国立民俗博物館の出入り口など3つの門が開放されていましたが、43年ぶりにヨンチュムン(迎秋門)が開放されたことで、東・西・南・北全ての門で出入りが可能となりました。 キョンボックン(景福宮)についてよくある質問 キョンボックン(景福宮)の定休日はいつですか？ キョンボックン(景福宮)の休館日は毎週火曜日です。 ただし、祝日と休館日が重なる日は開館し、開館した日の次の最初の開館日を休みとします。(2026年基準) 韓服を着ればキョンボックン(景福宮)を無料で観覧できますか？ はい。韓服を着用した方は、キョンボックン(景福宮)の入場が無料です。 韓服についての詳しい規定はガイドラインを参照してください。 キョンボックン(景福宮)の解説ツアーにはどうやって参加できますか？ 10名未満の観覧客は、別途の予約なしで解説ツアーに参加できます。10名以上の団体は予約が必要で、1回あたり30名まで予約が可能です。キョンボックン(景福宮)を見学しながら解説者の案内を聞くことができるキョンボックン(景福宮)の正規解説は、予約なしで参加できます。日本語の解説は毎日10:00/14:30に行われます。(火曜日を除く) 景福宮管理所の解説ツアーのページをみる

_raw_content.post_desc:
景福宫是朝鲜建国初期建造的第一座宫殿，迄今已有600年的历史。规模为五大宫殿之首，勤政殿、庆会楼等宫内建筑风格独特。此外，还建有国立古宫博物馆和国立民俗博物馆，游客可在此尽享游览之趣。每天上午10点至下午4点的整点时间，在景福宫兴礼门前，都会举行再现当时负责开关宫门、守卫及巡逻任务的守门将士守卫仪式和交接班仪式，游客可以一睹朝鲜时期守卫王宫将士们井然有序的仪式表演场景。

 

时隔43年，景福宫西门“迎秋门”于2018年12月再次开放。不仅方便西村地区游客进入参观景福宫，也藉此刺激西侧经济。在此之前，景福宫只开放了南门光化门(正门)、北门神武门，以及东侧国立民俗博物馆出入口。这次西门迎秋门开放后，东、西、南、北四个方向都能进出景福宫。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Namdaemun Market is the largest traditional market in Korea with over 10,000 stores that line the streets around Namdaemun (Gate), the main southern gate of the old city wall. Namdaemun Market first started under the reign of King Taejong (1367 – 1422, the third Joseon king) during the Joseon Dynasty (1392 – 1910), when the government built shops around Namdaemun and rented out the shops to traders. It boasts one of the largest distribution structures in Korea, providing local products, daily living essentials, food products, medical supplies and more to retailers and consumers across the country.


Due to the wholesale nature of the market, shoppers can comparison shop for the lowest prices on all sorts of goods. Namdaemun Market is also packed with interesting things to see and eat, making it a popular destination for both locals and international visitors alike. So whether you’re looking for traditional oriental medicine or imported drugs, traditional Korean food or imported snacks, hanbok attire or a Halloween costume, Namdaemun Market is the place to go.


Namdaemun Market is renowned for its vast size and the variety of goods it offers. With the exception of construction materials, the market sells nearly every item under the sun including clothing, food, living essentials, etc. So it comes as no surprise that Namdaemun Market is always bustling day and night. Retailers from all over the nation flock to the market at night and local consumers flock to the market during the day. Many tourists come during the day as well to experience the charm of a traditional Korean market. The market's success is largely due to its independent distribution system. Although the shops are small, most of them produce the goods they offer themselves, allowing for customers to purchase goods directly from the manufacturers at wholesale prices.


Frequently Asked Questions about Namdaemun Market

What is the nearest subway station to Namdaemun Market?

The nearest subway station to Namdaemun Market is Hoehyeon(Namdaemun Market) Station (Subway Line 4).

What are the opening hours of Namdaemun Market?

Namdaemun Market is open from 00:00 to 23:00 on weekdays, and opening hours may vary per stall.

Are there any tourist attractions worth visiting near Namdaemun Market?

Namdaemun Market has the following tourist attractions.

  • • Sungnyemun Gate (Namdaemun)

  • • Namsan Seoul Tower

  • • Deoksugung Palace

_raw_content.post_desc: The Seoul City Wall was originally built in 1396, surrounding Seoul (then known as  Hanyang) during the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1897). The wall stretches for 18.6km along the ranges of Bugaksan Mountain, Naksan Mountain, Namsan Mountain, and Inwangsan Mountain. The wall stands at average heights of 7 - 8 m high. Along the Seoul City Wall, there once stood eight gates that were originally built between 1396-1398, but only six remain standing. The North, South, East, and West gates of the wall are known as the “Four Great Gates” (Sukjeongmun, Heunginjimun, Sungnyemun, Dongeuimun), while the Northwest, Northeast, Southwest, and Southwest gates are known as the “Four Minor Gates” (Changuimun, Hyehwamun, Gwanghuimun, Soeuimun).

_raw_content.post_desc:
Opened in 1970, Dongdaemun Shopping Complex is the largest single market in Asia as well as one of the oldest with over 40 years of history. In 1985 Dongdaemun Shopping Town was added to the complex bringing the total to four buildings altogether (A, B, C and Shopping Town). This traditional market houses many wholesale and retail stores specializing in various fabrics, materials, accessories, and wedding products. As much as eighty percent of all the fabric traded in Korea goes through here, allowing for goods to be sold at reasonable prices. Dongdaemun Shopping Complex first opened with over 5,000 shops crammed into three separate buildings. Recently the market was extensively refurbished and extended to include outlets selling quilts, corsages and handmade toys.


Frequently Asked Questions about Dongdaemun Market?

What are the business hours of Dongdaemun Market?

Dongdaemun Market business hours vary by section.

  • • Fabric, clothing : 08:00 ~ 18:00 (Closed on Sundays)

  • • Accessories : 09:30 ~ 19:00 (Closed on Sundays)

  • • Wedding supplies and home interiors : 08:00 ~ 19:00 (Closed on the 2nd and 4th Sundays)

  • • Food Court in Building N, Restaurant District : 07:00 ~ 18:00 (Saturday: 07:00 ~ 17:00 / Closed on Sunday)

  • • Building B, Restaurant District : 08:00 ~ 19:00 (Closed on Sundays)


※ 2nd and 4th Sundays are all closed days.

Where can I park my car when visiting Dongdaemun Market?

You can park your car in the rooftop parking lot and underground parking lot of Dongdaemun Market.

What is the nearest subway station to Dongdaemun Market?

The nearest subway station to Dongdaemun Market is Dongdaemun Station (Subway Line 1,4 Exit 8, 9). Exit 9 is an underground connection to Dongdaemun Market. Please check the website below for more transportation information, including bus information.

Dongdaemun Market Transportation Guide

_raw_content.post_desc:
Changsin-dong Toy Wholesale Market is the largest toy and stationery market in Korea with over 100 stores. The market sells various toys, such as robots, dolls, kitchen sets etc, all sorts of stationery and party supplies. Stores in the market sell goods for an average of 30 to 40 percent less than in retail stores. Customers are able to get good quality toys and stationery made in Korea. Moreover, the toy market is within easy reach of Dongdaemun Fashion Street, Korea’s well-known shopping district, so it is perfect to combine visits at the same time. 


The wholesale toy market consists of stores lined up on both sides of the market's access road. The stores display piles of goods on stands outside the stores ready for their customers. The market is full to bursting with toys, such as robots, dolls, kitchen sets, educational toys, self-assembly toys and so on; in other words, it is a toys’ paradise.  Changsin-dong Toy Market is not only for children: adults enjoy how it brings back special memories of childhood and collectors in particular have great fun discovering hidden treasures.

_raw_content.post_desc:
The 63 Square skyscraper is a Yeouido landmark commanding spectacular views of the city. Standing 249 meters (817 ft) high and comprising of 60 floors and three basement levels, 63 Square is one of Korea’s tallest and most recognized buildings. The glass elevators which serve the viewing observatory ascend at a speed of 460 meters per minute, taking just 25 seconds to reach the top, giving passengers the sensation of a rocket-powered take-off as they enjoy breathtaking views. Aqua Planet 63, a major tourist attraction within 63 Square, ceased operations on June 30, 2024. Additionally, the observatory “63 Art,” where visitors could enjoy views of Seoul and art pieces, also ceased operations on the same day. In 2025, the Centre Pompidou Hanwha Seoul is scheduled to open in 63 Square.


63 Square’s distinctive gold color is the real thing; each of the 14,000 panes of glass was coated with a thin film of 24-carat gold which catches the sunshine, reflecting gold, red and silver as the sun sets, giving the tower its stunning multi-colored sheen.


Frequently Asked Questions about 63 Square
Are pets allowed in the 63 Square(63 Building)?
Pets are not allowed in all viewing areas within 63 Square(63 Building). (As of 2024)
Are there any tourist attractions worth visiting near 63 Square(63 Building)?
These are the following tourist attractions around 63 Square(63 Building).
National Assembly
Yeouido Hangang Park
Yeouido Saetgang Ecological Park

_raw_content.post_desc: ヨイド(汝矣島)のランドマークとなっている63 SQUAREは、地上60階、地下3階から成る超高層のアミューズメントビルです。抜群の眺望を誇る展望フロアをはじめ、水族館や公演会場など、多彩な施設を備えた複合空間になっています。63 SQUARE内の代表的な観光名所である「アクアプラネット63」は、2024年6月30日を基準に運営が終了しました。また、ソウルの全景と芸術作品を一緒に鑑賞することができる展望台「63アート」も運営が終了しました。63スクエアには、今後「ポンピドゥ・センター ハンファソウル」が2025年に開館する予定です。63 SQUARE最大の特徴は、ゴールドに光り輝くビルの壁面です。その壁面には、純度が最も高いK24を噴射コーティングした特殊ガラスを使用。使われた特殊ガラスの数は14,000枚で、ガラス1枚分の金の使用量は約0.36g。ビル全体では、なんと約5kgにも及ぶ金が使用されています。光の反射によって、金、銀、赤と様々な色に美しく変化する壁面は、ビルの外から見る「63 SQUARE」の見どころのひとつとなっています。またビルの60階にある展望台まで、分速460ｍの速度で一気に上昇する高速エレベーターも、韓国ドラマの撮影に使用されるなど、多くの話題を集めています。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Bukchon Hanok Village reflects 600 years of Seoul’s history. The village is situated between Gyeongbokgung Palace and Changdeokgung Palace, and its streets are lined with traditional hanok. Unlike other hanok villages (such as Namsangol Hanok Village), Bukchon was not created for tourists and it is a residential village inhabited by Seoulites. The best place within Bukchon to experience the old hanok atmosphere may be Gaehoe-dong. Here, hundreds of hanok sit shoulder to shoulder. Bukchon Hanok Village has been loved by many as a travel destination in Seoul as the charm of the traditional hanok is being rediscovered. There are also art galleries, traditional workshops, and restaurants that have been built out from from hanok, making these spaces both traditional and unique. In the Bukchon Hanok Village, which holds history and culture from time past in every alley, the Bukchon Cultural Center delivers information and cultural context for these traditional and historic spaces.


※ Measures to Take When Visiting Bukchon Hanok Village
• Due to the designation of Bukchon as a Special Management Area (Red Zone), tourist visiting hours will be restricted starting in November 2024. Please refer to the link below for more details.

View more →


•  Bukchon Hanok Village is a prominent residential area in Seoul, densely populated with hanoks where residents live.
Please keep this in mind and refrain from the following actions. We ask for your cooperation in practicing “silent tourism.”
- Please keep noise levels to a minimum, (e.g. no loud voices, horsing around, filming, etc.) especially in the 31 Gahoe-dong area
- Please do not litter
- Please keep group visits small, with a maximum of 10 visitors
- Please do not use microphones, megaphones, or loudspeakers
- Please do not take photos or film the interiors of houses, even if the doors are open

The cultural tours of the Bukchon Hanok Village area, (Gahoe-dong 31, 33, etc.) will be phased out. Please keep that in mind when taking the Seoul City Walking tours.

_raw_content.post_desc:
北村韩屋村位于景福宫，昌德宫和宗庙之间，是在首尔有着600年历史的韩国传统居住区。现在的北村并非是供游客观赏修建的民俗村，而是人们实际居住生活的村庄，而其中最著名的地方非嘉会洞31号路莫属。坐落于闹市区中的数百座韩屋，令游客叹为观止。随着韩屋画廊、传统作坊、韩屋餐厅等的入驻，这里更成为一个倍受瞩目的新文化艺术区。北屋韩屋村在现代与传统的结合中，仍然保留有象征朝鲜历史的遗迹与痕迹。不仅吸引着韩国的年轻人，更有大量的国内外游客前来参观。


※ 游览北村韩屋村的注意事项

• 根据北村特别管理地区（红色区域）的相关规定，自2024年11月起，将对游客的访问时间进行限制。具体详情请访问以下链接进行确认。

查看详情→


• 北村韩屋村作为首尔具有代表性的韩屋密集居住区，是当地居民实际居住的生活空间。请注意这一点，并克制以下行为，倡导进行“静默游”，以尊重当地居民的生活。
- 不要大声喧哗，拍照也尽量不要发出太大的噪音（尤其是嘉会洞31号等韩屋密集区）
- 不要随处乱扔垃圾，将垃圾带离韩屋区
- 团体游客尽量控制在10名左右
- 避免使用扩音器
- 不要在开着门的韩屋门前拍照

北村韩屋村最密集的路段（非嘉会洞31号路，33号路），将取消文化观光解说师，预约徒步观光时请注意。

_raw_content.post_desc: Namsangol Hanok Village is a collection of five hanok (traditional Korean houses) from the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910), recovered from different parts of the city and relocated to the northern foot of Namsan Mountain. The interiors of each of these five houses reflect owners from different walks of life, from the middle class to high government officials, noblemen and aristocrats. At Namsangol Hanok Village, visitors can see the hanok of important figures from the Joseon era including the house of Queen Yun's parents, who was the Queen Consort to King Sunjong, the 27th king of the Joseon Dynasty; the jaesil (study) of Yun Taekyeong, King Sunjong's father-in-law; the house of Min Yeong-hui, a relative of Empress Myeongseong; the house of Lee Seungeop, who was in charge of constructing Gyeongbokgung Palace and the house of Kim Chunyeong, a military official of the Joseon Dynasty. At the hanok village, international visitors can participate in traditional Korean activities such as archery and enjoy traditional Korean performances as well. Anyone who is curious about Korean wedding culture should visit the village on the weekend when traditional wedding ceremonies take place.

_raw_content.post_desc:
ナムサン・ハノンマウル(南山韓屋村)には、ソウル市内に点在していた韓国の伝統家屋5棟が移築されています。朝鮮王朝時代(1392～1910年)の貴族階級であるヤンバン(両班：朝鮮王朝時代の貴族階級)の屋敷のほか、一般的な伝統家屋が当時のままの姿を留めています。朝鮮王朝時代の南山一帯は、渓谷やチョンウガク(泉雨閣)という楼閣(四方を望めるように扉や壁をなくした高床式の建物)があり、夏の避暑地としても人気の高いスポットでした。ナムサン・ハノンマウル(南山韓屋村)では、その泉雨閣(チョンウガク)も復元。さらに谷や東屋なども設けられており、周囲に広がる美しい風景を眺めながら散策を楽しむことができます。ナムサン・ハノンマウル(南山韓屋村)では、韓国の伝統公演や弓矢撃ちなどの伝統遊びなどをいつでも体験することができます。また、韓国の伝統婚礼も実際に執り行われており、見学することも可能です。また、テコンドー演武公演や外国人のためのテコンドー体験プログラムも行っています。
1998年にナムサン・ハノンマウル(南山韓屋村)を造成するにあたり、散在していた5軒の伝統家屋を移転しました。ミョンソン(明成)皇后の親戚であるミン・ヨンフィ(閔泳徽)家屋、キョンボックン(景福宮)改築当時の棟梁であったイ・スンオプ(李承業)家屋、朝鮮王朝時代末期に五衛将の官職だったキム・チュンヨン(金春永)家屋などがあります。

_raw_content.post_desc:
As one of the most vibrant traditional markets in Seoul, Gwangjang Market is based in the center of the city so it can easily be located by even first-time visitors. This historic market opened in the early 20th century and is home to a number of clothing and food stalls, offering tourists a taste of traditional Korean cuisine. Starting with "addictive gimbap," one of Koreans’ all-time favorite snacks, and nokdujeon (mung bean pancake), visitors can sample a range of Korean delicacies. Other traditional treats such as tteok-bokki (stir-fried rice cake) and eomuk (fish cake) are also available. It is worth visiting the food stalls since most dishes are reasonably priced. If you have a keen interest in clothing, we recommend that you visit the hanbok stores and vintage clothing shops on the 2nd floor. 


Frequently Asked Questions about Gwangjang Market

What is the famous food in Gwangjang Market?

Favorite foods at Gwangjang Market include Bindae-tteok (Mung Bean Pancake,) Modum-jeon (Assorted Savory Pancakes,) Mayak Gimbab, Sundae (Korean Sausage) and Head Meat, Yukhoe (Beef Tartare ), and Korean style meatballs.

Where can I park my car when visiting Gwangjang Market?

When visiting Gwangjang Market, please use the Jongno 4-ga Jongmyo parking lot.

Are there any tourist attractions worth visiting Gwangjang Market?

There are the following tourist attractions around Gwangjang Market.

  • • Sewoon Shopping Center

  • • Jongmyo Shrine

  • • Dongdaemun Design Plaza

Huwon is self-contained and occupies sixty percent of Changdeokgung. The palace buildings are situated on the ridge of Bugaksan Mountain and have very few artificial features in order to blend into their natural surroundings. In the center of Huwon is a large pond, Buyongji, along with Buyongjeong Pavilion and Juhapru Pavilion. It is said that King Jeongjo (the twenty-second king of the Joseon Dynasty) and his courtiers often enjoyed fishing here at Buyongjeong.

_raw_content.post_desc:
Changdeokgung Palace is the second UNESCO World Heritage Site in Seoul. It was selected as a representative palace for its notable beauty in the history of palace architecture in East Asia and for its excellent arrangement with the surrounding naturalenvironment. Changdeokgung Palace was built by King Taejong in 1405.


During the Imjin War, Joseon lost both Gyeongbokgung Palace and Changdeokgung Palace. Reconstructed in the 2nd year of Gwanghaegun (1610), Changdeokgung was used as the royal palace of Joseon for about 270 years.


Changdeokgung Palace has two major tour programs. The first is the general tour, which is a basic tour that covers Injeongjeon (仁政殿), the main hall, and Nakseonjae (樂善齋). The second is a special tour of Howon, which runs from Buyongji, the entrance toHowon, to Okryucheon. The conservation of the ecosystem is absolutely stunning and includes various ponds and gardens.

朝鮮は壬辰倭乱（文禄·慶長の役）を経験し、キョンボックン(景福宮)とチャンドックン(昌徳宮)を全て失いました。クァンヘグン(光海君)2年(1610)に再建されたチャンドックン(昌徳宮)は約270年間朝鮮の法宮として使われました。


チャンドックン(昌徳宮)は大きく二つの観覧プログラムを持っています。 最初は一般観覧です。インジョンジョン(仁政殿を中心に楽善斎まで取り入れる基本的な観覧コースです。二つ目は後援特別観覧で後援の入り口から後援の白眉玉流川に至るコースです。生態系の保存状態が良く、池や庭園などには借景の跡が目立ちます。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Changgyeonggung Palace was built in 1483 by King Seongjong (the ninth king of the Joseon Dynasty) to take care of the wives of the preceding kings. Compared to other palaces, the size of the palace is compact and simple. Changgyeonggung Palaceis connected with Changdeokgung Palace. It's located east of the primary palace of Gyeongbokgung, so it is also referred to as "Donggwol," the "East Palace."

Myeongjeongjeon is the main hall of the palace, where state affairs were held, such as meetings with officials and the reception of foreign envoys. In particular, Myeongjeongjeon represents an outstanding example of seventeenth century Joseon architectural style and is the oldest main hall of any palace. While visiting Changgyeonggung Palace, it is recommended you visit nearby Changdeokgung Palace as well.

Most of the palace buildings were destroyed by the Japanese during the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592. The main buildings such as Myeongjeongjeon, Munjeongjeon (council hall), Hwangyeongjeon (Hall), Inyangjeon (Hall), Gongsacheong, and Honghwamun (Gate) were rebuilt by King Gwanghaegun (the fifteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty). During the Japanese occupation, the Japanese built a zoo on the site and renamed the palace "Changgyeongwon," meaning "Changgyeong Garden." Since 1987, the palace has been reconstructed and now resembles its original form.

_raw_content.post_desc: As a living vestige of Korea's history and culture, The National Museum of Korea is home to today's best collection of history and culture deeply rooted within the Korean people. Regular exhibitions and education programming speak of the numerous anecdotes of the nearly 420,000 collected historical artifacts with thousands of years of history, while also offering realistic digital animations and VR technology to provide a more impactful experience. The museum includes everything from a simple hand axe of the Paleolithic Period and a magnificient golden crown of the Three Kingdoms Period to Goryeo Period celadons, or pottery, and paintings dating back to the Joseon Period, as well as pictures of modern-era Korea and a variety of other zones dedicated to different cultures throughout the globe. Bring your family, friends, or even that special someone over to the museum for a day of fascination amid a compilation of detailed and colorful history.

_raw_content.post_desc:
Unhyeongung Palace is one of Seoul's smaller palaces and it is an important historic site that is open to the public. The palace was formerly the private residence of Emperor Gojong's father, the prince regent Heungseon Daewongun. The young Gojong lived here before he assumed the throne and his wedding to Myeongseong took place here. An annual re-enactment of the royal wedding ceremony between Emperor Gojong and Empress Myeongseong takes place here at the palace.


During the reign of Emperor Gojong, Unhyeongung was as grand as any other palace in Seoul, but over time, many of the palace buildings were heavily damaged and destroyed. Today, visitors can see what has been preserved of the palace and take part in traditional cultural activities and crafts experiences. On weekends, visitors can watch Seoulites get married in traditional Korean wedding ceremonies at the palace.

extra.cmmn_important:
ウンヒョングン(雲峴宮)は、コジョン(高宗：朝鮮王朝第26代国王)の父、フンソン・デウォングン(興宣大院君：1820～1898年)の自宅であり、コジョン(高宗)が生まれてから国王になる前まで暮らしていた家です。また、後にはコジョン(高宗)とミョンソン・ワンフ(明聖王后)の結婚式が行われた場所でもあります。コジョン(高宗)の時代には王宮に比較されるほどの規模を誇っていましたが、歴史的に多くの被害を受けたため、多くの建物は消失してしまいました。ここでは、毎年、コジョン(高宗)とミョンソン・ワンフ(明聖王后)の結婚式の様子を再現した行事が開催されます。また、この他にも多彩な宮廷文化に関連した行事が催され、韓国伝統の宮廷文化を体験するにおすすめのスポットです。近くにはインサドン(仁寺洞)通りやプクチョン(北村)韓屋村があるので一緒に楽しむのもおすすめです。

_raw_content.post_desc: Jongmyo is a royal shrine dedicated to the performance of ancestral rites for the deceased kings and queens of the Joseon Dynasty. Being the place where the royal ancestral tablets are enshrined, Jongmyo's atmosphere is solemn and sacred rather than splendid like the royal palaces. The simple and elegant buildings of this shrine have faithfully kept their original forms since the 16th century. Jongmyo is made up of Jeongjeon (the main hall), Yeongnyeongjeon (the hall of eternal peace), and auxiliary buildings such as Jeonsacheong, Eosuksil, Hyangdaecheong and Sindang. Jeongjeon, the main hall of Jongmyo, is a place steeped in royal history and is highly esteemed for its outstanding architecture. It is said to be the world's longest single wooden structure with a length measures 109 meters. The main hall is an outstanding example of traditional Korean architecture. Jongmyo was designated as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site together with Jongmyo Jerye and Jongmyo Jeryeak. Jongmyo Jerye is the royal ancestral ritual and has been performed for 600 years. The court music performed during the ritual is the Jongmyo Jeryeak.

_raw_content.post_desc: チョンミョ(宗廟)は、朝鮮王朝歴代の王と王妃のシンジュ(神主：位牌)、そしてヨンジョン(影幀：掛け軸に描かれた絵)を祀った王家の霊廟です。端麗な建物は、16世紀以降から現在まで、その原型をしっかり留めたままで保存されています。その卓越した建築様式と歴史的な価値が認められ、チョンミョ(宗廟)は1995年にユネスコ世界文化遺産に指定されました。また、チョンミョ(宗廟)で600年の間、継承された祭礼儀式の「チョンミョ・チェレ(宗廟祭礼)」は、韓国の重要無形文化財第56号に、そして祭礼の時に使われた音楽の「チョンミョ・チェレアク(宗廟祭礼楽)」は重要無形文化財第1号に指定され、ユネスコ世界無形文化遺産にもそれぞれ指定されています。

_raw_content.post_desc: 宗庙是供奉朝鲜王朝历代国王和王妃牌位的王家祠堂，建筑风格非常肃穆和庄重。宗庙分正殿和偏殿，偏殿包括永宁殿、典祀厅、御肃室、香大厅、神堂等。其核心建筑是供奉神位、进行祭祀的正殿，里面沉睡着悠久的王家历史。它长达109米，是世界上最长的单一建筑。宗庙、流传600年的祭祀仪式——宗庙祭礼、祭礼时的音乐——“宗庙祭礼乐”其价值被世界认可，入选了联合国教科文组织世界文化遗产名录。

_raw_content.post_desc:
One of the five grand palaces, Gyeonghuigung Palace was also called "Seogweol" (which means "palace of the west") because it's located west of the main palace, Gyeongbokgung. In its heyday, it was part of a vast complex, with 100 buildings in total, but most of these were destroyed during the Japanese occupation. Following intensive restoration work, it reopened to the public in 2002. On its grounds stand the Seoul Museum of History and the Gyeonghuigung Annex Building of the Seoul Museum of Art.  The palace was originally constructed by order of King Gwanghae, the fifteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty, and was completed in 1623. From the beginning, it was much-loved and served as a secondary palace for some ten kings of the Joseon Dynasty. 

A variety of Korean art can also be seen in the Gyeonghuigung Annex building of the Seoul Museum of Art, which is situated on the Gyeonghuigung site. Also, the Seoul Museum of History, one of the foremost tourist attractions in the city, houses a permanent collection allowing visitors to see how Seoul has developed and transformed from prehistoric times to the present day.

_raw_content.post_desc: キョンヒグン(慶熙宮)は朝鮮王朝15代国王であるクァンヘグン(光海君)が建築を進め、1623年に完成しました。当時のキョンヒグン(慶熙宮)には卓越した建物が多く見られ、創建以降は約280年間、10代に渡る歴代の国王達が離宮として愛用していました。しかし、数々の受難に見舞われ、19世紀にキョンボックン(景福宮)が改築された際には、キョンヒグン(慶熙宮)にあった多くの建物が景福宮へと移築されました。 また日本統治時代の1910年にはキョンソン(京城)中学校の建設が進められ、それまで残っていた重要な史蹟なども大部分を撤去、面積も半分ほどに縮小されました。その後、1987年からソウル市によるキョンヒグン(慶熙宮)復元事業で主要な殿閣を復元。2002年からは一般公開されています。ソウル歴史博物館、ソウル市立美術館キョンヒグン(慶熙宮)分館などが隣接しており、見どころも満載です。

extra.cmmn_important: Rakgojae is a traditional cultural experience center where visitors can stay in a traditional hanok and enjoy traditional food, music, and dance. Built in an “ㅁ” shape around a central courtyard, Rakgojae faithfully recreates the refined lifestyle of the yangban aristocracy of the past. The beauty of traditional architecture is enhanced by the natural charm of the tiled walls, pavilions, ponds, jar racks, and chimneys, as well as the pine trees and bamboo scattered among the hanok buildings. Visitors can also experience Korean traditional culture, including traditional cuisine and tea ceremonies, as well as performances of traditional Korean music such as daegeum and pansori. However, Rakgojae is rented out as an entire house for groups of 5–9 people, and the price is comparable to that of a hotel. Agungi Jjimjilbang: Rakgojae features an Agungi Jjimjilbang. Overnight guests can use it free of charge. The unique warmth of the ondol heating system is another charm of the hanok for foreign tourists. Exclamations of “Wonderful!” keep coming out.

_raw_content.post_desc: Rakkojae is a beautiful hanok guesthouse and restaurant that is located near Anguk Station. Built over 130 years ago, Rakkojae's main building was once a Korean cultural academy. The building has undergone subsequent renovation and was remodeled into its current form by Jeong Yeongjin who holds the designation of Master Carpenter of Human Cultural Properties. At Rakkojae's restaurant, visitors can enjoy Korean food, a tea drinking ceremony, Korean folk music and dance in the picturesque setting of a traditional hanok. Advance reservations are required to dine at Rakkojae. Experience Seoul in a beautiful traditional hanok!

The market slowly started to establish itself in the late 1960s when small medicinal herbs stores started opening one by one. Today, the market has grown to become the nation's largest oriental medicine market, and 70 percent of the oriental medicine traded in Korea goes through here. Because the market is able to minimize distribution costs, the medicinal herbs sold here cost around 30 percent cheaper than elsewhere.

More than 800 oriental medicine shops and clinics are located in this area.

_raw_content.post_desc: ソウルヤンニョン(薬令)市場は韓国で最も大きい漢方薬市場。約800カ所を超える韓方薬関連店舗を確保しています。韓国全土の薬剤という薬材はすべてここに集まります。1960年代、ソウルヤンニョン(薬令)市場は韓薬材の商人たちが韓国全土からチョンニャン(清凉里)駅を利用して集まり始めたことで自然的に始まりました。ここでは各種民間療法に登場するカエル、スッポン、淡水エビなど珍しい薬剤も購入でき、煎じ薬屋があって手数料1万ウォン程度さえ支払えば、薬が飲みやすいように密封包装してくれます。また、高麗人参市場では、高麗人参、紅参、米参と様々な蜂蜜、韓国産霊芝キノコなどが販売されています。最近は外国人の足も増えています。まだ高麗人参を買う程度にとどまっていますが、彼らにとっては買い物に出かけ、珍しい見どころとしての魅力も大きいです。手頃な価格のほか、田舎の市場に来たかのように、ソウルヤンニョン(薬令)市場は四季折々の人々でにぎわっています。

_raw_content.post_desc: Simujang, the residence of Manhae Han Yong-un, was built in 1933 during the Japanese occupation. Unlike typical hanok homes that face south, this house faces north. As an independence activist, Manhae chose a north-facing site on the hillside to avoid facing the Japanese Government-General of Korea. The house has a rectangular layout with a hip-and-gable roof and features four front rooms and two side rooms. Inside, you’ll find Manhae's personal room with preserved artifacts such as his calligraphy, research papers, and court records from his time in prison. After his death, his only daughter, Han Young-sook, lived there. However, when the Japanese Embassy moved across from the property, she relocated to Myeongnyun-dong, and Simujang was transformed into a research center dedicated to Manhae's philosophy.

_raw_content.post_desc: 万海ハン・ヨンウン(韓龍雲)シムジャン(尋牛荘)は、日本統治時代の1933年に万海ハン・ヨンウン(韓龍雲)が建てた家で、一般的な韓屋が南向きであるのに対し、珍しく北向きに建てられています。彼は独立運動家であり、南向きに建てると朝鮮総督府と向き合うことになるため、山の斜面の北向きの土地を選びました。正面が4間、側面が2間の形をしており、入母屋造りの韓屋の伝統的な木造建築様式の家です。ハン・ヨンウン(韓龍雲)が使っていた部屋には、彼の書や研究論文集、獄中公判記録などがそのまま保存されています。彼の死後も一人娘のハン・ヨンスク(韓英淑)が住んでいましたが、日本大使館が向かいに位置するようになると、ミョンニュンドン(明倫洞)に引っ越し、シムジャン(尋牛荘)は万海の思想研究所として使用されることになりました。

_raw_content.post_desc: 万海韩龙云寻牛庄是1933年建造的房屋，那时正值日本帝国主义强占时期。这座房子由万海韩龙云所建，在偏爱南向的韩屋中颇为罕见。作为独立运动家的他，若选择南向，其住所将与朝鲜总督府正面相对，因此他选择了位于山坡北向的位置。布局为正面四间、侧面两间的长方形平面，其上搭建了八角屋顶，这里是民道里小鲁收藏家的所在地。在韩龙云曾经使用过的房间里，至今完整地保存着他的笔迹、研究论文集以及狱中公判记录等珍贵物品。去世后，他的独生女韩英淑继续居住在这里。然而，当日本大使馆官邸在对面落成后，她搬离了寻牛庄，迁往明伦洞。此后，寻牛庄被用作万海的思想研究所。

_raw_content.post_desc: The Heo Jun Museum commemorates the life and works of the renowned Joseon-era doctor and scholar, Heo Jun. The museum is located in Gayang-dong near Guam Park and the neighborhood is known as the birthplace of Heo Jun. Visitors can see a range of items relating to Oriental medicine, items once owned by Heo Jun, and medical books. Some of the books on display were written out by Heo Jun's hand. A writing model of his most famous work, "Dongui Bogam," is on display and it is still an influential medical tome in Oriental medicine today.

_raw_content.post_desc: ソンジョンヌン(宣靖陵)は「ソンルン(宣陵)」と「ジョンルン(靖陵)」を合わせた呼称。ソンルン(宣陵)は朝鮮王朝第9代王ソンジョン(成宗：在位1469～1494年)の陵とソンジョン(成宗)の3番目の王后であるチョンヒョンワンフ(貞顕王后：1462～1530年)の陵です。そして、息子である第11代王チュンジョン(中宗：在位1506～1544年)の陵がジョンルン(靖陵)。ソンジョンヌン(宣靖陵)は2009年にユネスコ世界文化遺産に登録されてその地位を一層高めました。地下鉄2号線ソンルン駅に隣接しているためアクセスが便利で、散歩を楽しむ市民にも人気の場所です。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Seoul Folk Flea Market is the largest flea market in Korea. The market sells typical Korean items, everyday goods, souvenirs, traditional goods and traditional food, allowing visitors to enjoy shopping and eating all under one roof. These days, the market has become one of the city's main attractions among local people as well as overseas visitors. Seoul Folk Flea Market is filled with Korean traditional goods and foods that reflect the simpler lifestyle of Koreans in times past. The market  opened in April 2008 and is a place alive with typical Korean folk items, souvenirs, traditional food and everyday goods that reveal the lifestyle of Koreans in times past. The market holds performances of "Pungmulpae" (pungmul band, traditional Korean percussion band) all year round. Regional specialties and traditional and modern crafts are also bought and sold here. In this two-story building, everyday miscellaneous goods, antiques and clothing are found on the first floor, and restaurants are situated on the second floor. 


Seoul Folk Flea Market is divided into seven zones; red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet, the colors of rainbow. The red zone is a food court. The orange zone is for regional specialties such as squid from Ulleungdo Island, traditional crafts like crockery, and bits and bobs such as smoking pipes etc. The yellow zone deals with secondhand vintage goods, such as typewriters, telephones etc. The green zone is for antiques, such as traditional antique furniture and art. The blue zone sells fashion accessories and the indigo zone sells clothing, paintings, calligraphy, hanji (traditional handmade Korean paper) and so on. Finally, the violet zone displays and sells miscellaneous goods, electronics, tools etc. The market has many rare goods that cannot easily be found elsewhere.

_raw_content.post_desc: Seodaemun Prison was used to intern Korean patriots during the Japanese occupation. Until the Liberation of Korea on August 15, 1945, it was known as a clandestine mecca for the anti-Japanese resistance fighters, where they were tortured and executed. The Seodaemun Prison History Hall opened in November 1998 in Seodaemun Independence Park to commemorate the patriots who sacrificed their lives in the fight for Korean independence during the Japanese occupation. It consists of a historic exhibition hall, a central prison, jail cells, a hospital, the patriot memorial, an execution room, a tunnel through which corpses were carried, a watchtower, and a basement jail cell where the female patriot, Yu Gwansun, was tortured and killed.

_raw_content.post_desc: King Taejo of the Joseon Dynasty moved the capital to Hanyang in 1394 and built Gyeongbokgung Palace, the official residence of the Joseon Dynasty. In addition, on both sides of the road in front of the palace’s main gate, the Street of Six Ministries, including Uijeongbu (State Council), was built. It was the best road in Hanyang. In 2009, that road opened again. Gwanghwamun Square and Cheonggye Plaza were built. The square is mostly “a square that restores the history of Gwanghwamun,” “a square that recreates the scenery of the Street of the Six Ministries,” “an emblematic square of Korea,” “an urban culture square where citizens mingle,” “a square in the city center,” and “a connection to the Cheonggyecheon Stream.” It functions as a space for history, culture, and relaxation. The focal point of this emblematic square in Korea is the statue of King Sejong the Great. The “downtown square” around the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin is also a space appreciated by city dwellers. In addition, artificial ponds and fountains are installed to cool off people from the summer heat. Also, the Haechi statue and Grass Plaza, which are symbols of Seoul, were also created.

_raw_content.post_desc: 朝鮮太祖は、1394年に都をハニャン(漢陽)に移し、政局のキョンボックン(景福宮)を建てました。そして、宮殿の正門であるクァンファムン(光化門)前の道の左右に議政府を含めて六朝官衙通りを建設しました。クァンファムン(光化門)からチョンゲ(清渓)広場に至る広場ができ、2009年にその道が、再び開かれました。広場は大きく「クァンファムン(光化門)の歴史を回復する広場」、「六朝通りの風景を再現する広場」、「韓国を代表する広場」、「市民が参加する都市文化広場」、「都心の中の広場」、「チョンゲチョン(清渓川)連結部」に分けれています。歴史性と文化、休息の空間として機能を持ち、特に「韓国を代表する広場」は、セジョン(世宗)大王銅像があり、広場の中心としての役割を果たしています。イ・スンシン(李舜臣)将軍銅像の銅像周辺部である「都心の中の広場」も市民に愛される空間で、人工池や噴水を設置し、夏場には市民の暑さを和らげてくれます。この他にもソウル市の象徴であるハッチの造形物や芝生の広場も作られました。

_raw_content.post_desc: Bosingak Pavilion, a bell tower located in Jongno 2-ga, Jongno-gu, was the original site of the Old Bronze Bell (Treasure No.2). Due to cracks that rendered the bell unringable, it is now housed at the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan. The current bell hanging in Bosingak Pavilion is a newly cast replica, funded through public donations. It was installed on August 14, 1985, and first rung the following day, August 15. Bosingak Pavilion is renowned for hosting Korea’s iconic New Year’s Eve bell-ringing ceremony, where the bell is struck 33 times at midnight on December 31. Additionally, the bell is rung 12 times daily at noon, except on Mondays.

_raw_content.post_desc: ポシンガク(普信閣)は、チョンノ区チョンノ2ガ(鍾路2街)にある鐘楼で、宝物第2号であるソウルポシンガク(普信閣)鐘があった場所です。現在、ポシンガク(普信閣)鐘は亀裂が入ってしまい、鳴らすことができないため、ヨンサン(龍山)にある国立中央博物館で保管されています。現在ポシンガク(普信閣)に掛かっている鐘は、国民の寄付によって新しく鋳造されたものです。この鐘は1985年8月14日に初めてポシンガク(普信閣)に掛けられ、翌日の8月15日に初めて鳴らされました。ポシンガク(普信閣)では、韓国の代表的な年越し行事である、除夜の鐘が毎年行われています。除夜の鐘は毎年12月31日に33回鐘を打つ行事です。また、普段も月曜日を除いて毎日正午に12回鐘を鳴らしています。

_raw_content.post_desc: 宫中饮食研究院是专业传授列入国家重要非物质文化遗产第38号的“朝鲜王朝宫中饮食”的教育机构，是韩国饮食的代表。朝鲜王朝最后一位厨房尚宫韩熙顺的手艺得以完整传承。宫中饮食研究院面向公众开设宫中饮食培训讲座，参加者可以通过学习宫中饮食课程、传统饮食课程、宾馆韩定食课程等，学习韩国传统饮食的烹饪方法。研究院还开设“饮食文化体验课程”，旨在加强人们对韩国饮食的正确理解，普及饮食文化礼仪和风尚，弘扬韩国饮食作为减肥、健康饮食的优越性，推动韩国饮食走向世界。

_raw_content.post_desc: Heunginjimun Gate is a major historical site in Seoul. More commonly known as Dongdaemun Gate (Great Eastern Gate), it was designated treasure no. 1 by the Korean government. During the Joseon Dynasty, Heunginjimun Gate was one of eight city gates along the historic Seoul City Wall and it served as the main gate for the eastern part of the city. Heunginjimun is known for its exquisite architecture and beauty; the gate is also a spectacular sight at night. After viewing Heunginjimun, visitors may want to explore the Dongdaemun neighborhood and do some late-night shopping.

_raw_content.post_desc: フンインジムン(興仁之門)(通称トンデムン(東大門))は、韓国の宝物第1号です。朝鮮王朝時代(1392～1910年)、重要な国家施設があったハンソンブ(漢城府：現在のソウル都心部)を保護するソウル城郭に設置された、8つの城門のうち都の東側に建てられた大門です。フンインジムン(興仁之門)は、朝鮮王朝後期の建築様式の特徴である繊細で華麗な様がよく表れています。朝鮮王朝時代、城郭に設置された他の門とフンインジムン(興仁之門)が異なる点は、オンソン(甕城)があることです。オンソン(甕城)は城門を強化するため、門の外にもう一重設置した小さな城のことで、城門を敵から防御するためにとても有効な構造物です。フンインジムン(興仁之門)は美しくライトアップされる夜の姿も見どころのひとつです。フンインジムン(興仁之門)の夜景を観たあとは、周辺のトンデムン(東大門)入口に広がるファッション・タウンでショッピングを楽しむのもおすすめです。

_raw_content.post_desc: The Tteok Museum is a museum and experience center where visitors can learn about traditional Korean food. Permanent Exhibition Hall No. 1 showcases the different tteok (rice cakes) that were prepared and eaten on Korean holidays. Also on display are the various tools that were needed to create the tteok. Permanent Exhibition Hall No. 2 has displays on the tteok that were eaten during the daily life of a Korean person. From birth, to death, and all the occasions in between, the tteok that were or are served are on display at the Tteok Museum. The museum also offers classes on how to make tteok and other traditional Korean food.

_raw_content.post_desc:
Deoksugung Palace is unique among Korean palaces in having a modern seal engraving and a western style garden and fountain. Medieval and modern style architecture exists together in harmony in Deoksugung Palace. The Changing of the Royal Guard can be seen in front of Daehanmun (Gate) and is a very popular event for many visitors. During the Joseon Dynasty, the royal guard was responsible for opening and closing the palace gate as well as patrolling around the gate area. Outside the palace is a picturesque road flanked by a stone wall which is much loved by visitors.


Originally, Deoksugung Palace was not a palace. The Imjin War (the Japanese invasions in 1592) left all the palaces in Korea severely damaged. When King Seonjo (the fourteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty) returned to Seoul from his evacuation, the primary palace Gyeongbokgung Palace had been burnt to the ground and other palaces were also heavily damaged. A temporary palace was chosen from among the houses of the royal family. This is the origin of Deoksugung Palace. King Gwanghaegun (the fifteenth king of the Joseon Dynasty) named the palace Gyeongungung, formalizing it as a royal palace. Since then it has been used as an auxiliary palace by many Joseon kings. In 1897, Emperor Gojong (the twenty-sixth king of the Joseon Dynasty) stayed here and expanded it. The modern buildings such as Seokjojeon (Hall) were constructed during this period. In 1907, the palace was renamed Deoksugung.

_raw_content.post_desc: トクスグン(徳寿宮)に入るため、テピョンノ(太平路)の象徴であるテハンムン(大漢門)を通ります。しかし、元の位置ではありません。日本統治時代によってテピョンノ(太平路)が作られ、トクスグン(徳寿宮)の広さは減り、テハンムン(大漢門)も後に下がりました。1968年、テピョンノ(太平路)が拡張され、再び後に退き、現在の場所に戻りました。なんとなく広いテピョンノ(太平路)が無関心です。 テハンムン(大漢門)を過ぎて直進すると、チュンファムン(中和門) (宝物第819号)に着きますトクスグン(徳寿宮)の正殿であるチュンファジョン(中和殿)入口に当たります。チュンファジョン(中和殿)の前には品階石が並んであります。宮殿内の木造重層の石御堂も注目に値します。文禄•慶長の役の時に還都したソンジョ(宣祖)が泊まって崩御した場所であり、インジョバンジョン(仁祖反正)の後、クァンヘグン(光海君)が流弊した場所です。水時計のある報漏閣自擊漏(国宝第229号)は宮内唯一の国宝ですトクスグン(徳寿宮)の中には最初の西洋式建築物である石造殿がありますが、20世紀初めに建てられ、現在はトクスグン(徳寿宮)美術館として使われています。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Samcheongdong is Seoul's most stylish neighborhood, located just past Gyeongbokgung Palace's stone wall lined street. The name "Samcheong" is derived from the words "sam" meaning “three", and "cheong" meaning "fresh" or "pure", because the mountain, water and the heart of the people in this area are all very fresh and pure. Then it's not wonder why many artists have sought out Samcheong-dong over the years. Because of this, Samcheong-dong became known as an artistic area.


The area of Samcheongdong is actually made up of several neighborhoods: Anguk-dong, Sogyeok-dong, Hwa-dong, and Sagan-dong and ends at Samcheong Park. Samcheong-dong is dotted with various art museums, museums, art galleries, restaurants, cafés, and shops; some are traditional, some are modern, but all are unique and colorful.

_raw_content.post_desc: The Amsa-dong Prehistoric Settlement Site is a historic site where visitors can learn about Korea during the Neolithic era. The site has two exhibition halls with displays of ancient artifacts excavated at Amsa, and with educational displays about the lives of pre-historic people who lived during 5,000 BCE. Carbonized acorns, fishing net weights, and stone tools have been excavated at Amsa. Twenty five hut sites have been uncovered during excavations throughout the years and a total of nine huts have been restored to date.​

_raw_content.post_desc:
Banpodaegyo Bridge is a two-tiered bridge over the Han River that features the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, (the world’s longest bridge fountain recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records) with 380 water jets and a dazzling array of multi-colored lights. The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain’s water jets are dynamic and can move in time to music creating spectacular ever-changing displays. Add to that the hundreds of rainbow-colored lighting combinations when night falls, and it is easy to see why Banpodaegyo Bridge is a magnet for tourists year round.

The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain operates from April to October every year, however the schedule of the fountain shows varies from month to month. Each fountain show lasts 20 minutes. In addition, Banpo Hangang Park hosts the "Moonlight Square Cultural Weekend" event every Saturday from 7:00 - 8:30 p.m. from May to October, featuring a variety of musical styles including classical music with commentary, acappella, popera, jazz, brass bands and orchestras.


Frequently Asked Questions about Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain
What are Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain's operating hours?
The Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain operates in an increment of 20 minutes, and the operating hours are as follows. (As of 2024)

• Low season (April-June, September-October): 12:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:30, 21:00
• Peak season (July-August): 12:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:30, 21:00, 21:30

※ Fountain operation may be suspended depending on weather conditions (rain, strong wind) and the number of visitors in the park. (Fountain shutdown conditions: When predicting precipitation during the fountain's operating hours (※ In the case of a clear day after rain, the facility will be inspected and operated when there are no abnormalities (to prevent malfunction due to humidity), when there is a strong wind of 7m/s or more, and when the opacity of the Han River is 15NTU or more)

You can check the details of the Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain music production on the page below. (As of 2022)

Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain Song Information

The parking lots near Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain are as follows. Please check the following website for parking rates and real-time parking availability.

• Banpo 1 Parking Lot (122-1 Jamwon-dong, Seocho-gu, Seoul)
• Banpo 2 and 3 parking lot (115-5 Banpo-dong, Seocho-gu, Seoul)

_raw_content.post_desc: パンポデギョ(盤浦大橋)は、ハンガン(漢江)に架かる2層式の橋梁。2層のうち1層は、梅雨時期などに漢江が増水した際には浸水するよう設計され、「チャムスギョ(浸水橋)」とも呼ばれています。「月光虹噴水」はパンポデギョ(盤浦大橋)に設けられた380個のノズルから単に水を噴射するだけでなく、噴水が音楽に合わせてリズミカルに躍動する演出が施されています。昼には約100パターンの迫力ある噴水パフォーマンスを、また夜になれば約200個の照明が虹色に輝く光の演出も加わり、ロマンチックな水と光のショーを楽しむことができます。「世界で最も長い橋梁噴水」としてギネスブックにも登録されています。

_raw_content.post_desc: Taereung and Gangneung Royal Tombs are the burial sites of royalty from the Joseon Dynasty. Located in Hwarang-dong, Taereung and Gangneung sit next to each other. The Korea National Training Center for Sports sits between the two royal tombs and the center is operated by the Korean Olympic Committee. Taereung is the royal tomb of Queen Munjeong; the second wife of the 11th Joseon king, Jungjong. Gangneung is the royal tomb of the Queen Munjeong's son and the 13th Joseon king, Myeongjong and his wife, Queen Insun. In June 2009, all 40 of the royal tombs of the Joseon Dynasty were designated UNESCO World Heritage sites.

_raw_content.post_desc: Yonsei University is one of Korea's best universities. Its history is deep and many of the buildings on the Yonsei campus have modern historical significance as they were built in the early years of the 20th century. Stimson Hall was the first building ever built on the Yonsei campus and it was constructed in 1920. The hall was designated Historic Site No. 275 in 1981. Underwood Hall, Historic Site No. 276, was the second building ever built at Yonsei University. Today the hall functions as a museum dedicated to the founder of Yonsei, Horace G. Underwood and the Underwood family. Appenzeller Hall was built in 1924 and holds the designation of Historic Site No. 277. The hall was built to commemorate Henry Appenzeller who established the famed Korean boys' school, Paichai Hakdang.

_raw_content.post_desc: The Bangi-dong Ancient Baekje Tombs are ancient tombs in located the Bangi-dong area that date back to the Hanseong Baekje era. The ancient Hanseong Baekje Kingdom was founded along the Hangang River in 18 BCE and lasted for nearly 5 centuries. The tombs were discovered in the 1970s during the Jamsil District Zoning Project and there are 8 tombs altogether. Unfortunately, most of the artifacts were stolen at some point in time, but the tombs themselves were preserved well. Visitors can observe the original structures of the tombs and learn more about Hanseong Baekje. These ancient tombs are an important historical site and the area around the tombs was made into a park. There are paths between the tombs and visitors can take a quiet walk around the park and observe the tombs while enjoying the park's fresh air and grass. The site holds the designation of Historic Site No. 270.

_raw_content.post_desc: The Choonwondang Museum of Korean Medicine first opened in 2008 and is dedicated to hanbang, also known as Oriental medicine. The museum spans 7 floors, from the B1 level to the 6th floor and there are exhibitions halls, a decocting room, a quality inspection facility, a cultural space, a doctor’s office and an infirmary. The museum's exhibition halls display various historical artifacts relating to Oriental medicine. Display pieces date from the Three Kingdoms era to the Joseon Dynasty. The museum is gaining popularity as a new cultural venue where people can learn about Korean culture and hanbang.

_raw_content.post_desc:
The Seoul Museum of History is the only museum in Korea that represents the city’s history and culture. Since its establishment on the former site of Gyeonghuigung Palace in 2002, the museum has offered visitors the chance to experience 600 years of Seoul’shistoryand culture through interactive exhibitions. The three-story museum is divided thematically into three exhibition areas, including a special exhibition area, a permanent exhibition area and a hall that exhibits collections donated by the public.


The museum offers accessible and interactive exhibitions to the public with various hands-on programs. For example, visitors are allowed to touch and explore the exhibits on display, which are replicas of originals in the museum. In addition, the museumoffersthe U-Exhibit Guidance System, an automatic translator (various languages are available) for visitors, which makes every tour convenient and interesting.

_raw_content.sumry: Located in Buam-dong, Changuimun Gate is one of the four minor city gates of Seoul.

extra.cmmn_important: Built during the Joseon Dynasty, the Hanyangdoseong, Seoul City Wall once circled the entire city of Seoul. Now centuries old, much of the wall is still walkable today. _raw_content.post_desc: Bonghwanggak Pavilion was constructed in 1912 by Son Byeonghui, the Korean independence activist. Bongwhanggak was built to be an educational facility that taught students the doctrines of Cheondogyo and educated leaders of the Korean independence movement. Cheondogyo is a Korean religion founded by Choe Je-U and its main tenet is that life and death are one, and all things in the universe repeat in an endless cycle. "Bonghwang" is the Korean word for the phoenix and it appeared often in Choe's writings, which is how the pavilion came to be named Bonghwanggak. The pavilion is considered the main shrine of Cheondogyo. In 1969, Bongwhanggak was designated Tangible Cultural Property No. 2 by the Seoul Metropolitan Government.

_raw_content.post_desc: Jeongneung is the royal tomb of Queen Sindeok. She was the second wife of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty. It is said that the tomb was originally located behind Deoksugong (Palace) but moved to the current location when a son of King Taejo's first wife, King Taejong ( the third king of the Joseon Dynasty) ascended the throne. The original scale of the tomb was reduced as well. Although it is a simple tomb without many of the stone figures traditionally placed before a royal tomb, it has historical interest as it has faithfully kept the style of an early Joseon period tomb. The tomb is in picturesque surrounds with Bukhansan National Park located nearby.

_raw_content.post_desc: Tangchundaeseong Fortress was built in 1712 during the Joseon Dynasty to improve the defense of Hanyangdoseong, the Seoul City Wall, and the Bukhansanseong Fortress. Hongjimun Gate was built during the reign of King Sukjong, the 19th king of the Joseon Dynasty. Legend has it that King Sukjong wrote “Hongjimun” on the gate's original name-board himself and the gate was called Hongjimun thereafter. After passing through Hongjimun Gate, Tangchundaeseong Fortress comes into view. These days, the Tangchundaeseong area offers one of the most beloved hiking trails in Seoul. The hiking trail has a gentle slope for leisurely walks.

_raw_content.post_desc: Wongudan was built during the Joseon Dynasty to be an altar for performing divine harvest rituals. Located in central Seoul right near City Hall, it was designated Historic Site No. 157 in 1967. Through the past few centuries the altar was once called Hwandan and more recently Hwangudan. Now officially known as Wongudan Altar, Wongudan is located in close proximity to other major Seoul tourist attractions so it's convenient and easy to add a stop to Wongudan on a Seoul travel itinerary. The current Hwangudan Altar is a complex established in 1897 on the site of the old Nambyeolgung Palace. Its altar was built for Emperor Gojong's enthronement ceremony and rituals. The Japanese demolished the original complex in 1913, and a railway hotel was built on the site, reducing its size. Today, only the Hwangungu, the stone drum, and a stone gate with three arches remain preserved within the grounds of the Joseon Hotel.

_raw_content.post_desc: Sayuksin Park is located atop a hill between the Hangang River and Noryangjin Station. The park encompasses the historic Sayuksinmyo Tombs and the surrounding hilly area. The tombs hold the designation of Seoul Cultural Asset No. 8 and they are the burial site of seven Korean loyalists to the King Danjong, 6th king of the Joseon Dynasty. King Danjong was forced to abdicate by his uncle, who then assumed to the throne to become King Sejo. Seong Sam-Mun, Park Paeng-Nyeon, Ha Wi-Ji, Yi Gae, Yu Seong-Won, Yu Eung-Bu, and Kim Mun-Gi who opposed King Sejo and were buried here by the Hangang River.

_raw_content.post_desc:
Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon are the burial site of members of the Korean royal family and the site was designated Historic Site No. 361 in 1991. Yeonghwiwon is the royal tomb of Princess Consort Sunheon, wife of the 26th king of the Joseon Dynasty, Gojong. Sunginwon is the burial place of Crown Prince Yi Jin, grandson of King Gojong and Princess Consort Sunheon. 

In Korea, tombs for kings and queens are traditionally called “neung” and tombs of princes and royal consorts are called “won”. Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon were once known as Hongneung as Queen Myeongseong, the first wife of King Gojong was entombed here. The grave was moved to Geumgok-dong in the city of Namyangju in 1919 following the death of King Gojong. Since then, the site has been known as Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon. Apart from its historic significance, the greenery and beautiful surroundings here have always attracted sightseers.

_raw_content.post_desc: The Seoul Yangnyeongsi Herb Medicine Museum was established to preserve and pass on the history and knowledge of traditional Korean medicine. Fittingly, the museum is located across from the Seoul Yangnyeong Market, one of the most famous oriental medicine markets in Korea from which approximately 70% of the nation's oriental medicine is distributed. The museum collects, manages, and stores many artifacts and materials to exhibit. Visitors will be able to see everything from the herbs and plants used in traditional medicine, to antique medical records and tools. Admission to the museum is free.

_raw_content.post_desc: The name "Cheongwon Sanbang" is derived from Shim Yong-sik's carpenter's pen name "Cheongwon" and means "clear and round." Still making all the doors by hand in a traditional way, the center is dedicated to researching and preserving the window-knitting art, the face of hanok architecture. _raw_content.post_desc: Uireung is the royal tomb of King Gyeongjong, the 20th king of the Joseon dynasty, and his wife Queen Seonui. Uireung is located inside the Korea National University of Arts campus in Seokgwan-dong, Seongbuk-gu. Most royal tombs are "ssangneung," tombs that are arranged with the king and queen next to each other. At Uireung, the tombs of the king and the queen are arranged front to back. The tomb in the front is Queen Seonui’s and the one in the back belongs to King Gyeongjong. Uireung is closed Mondays.

_raw_content.post_desc: Heonilleung is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the final resting place of two pairs of the Joseon Dynasty's kings and queens. The name of the site is a combination of the names of the two separate tombs, Heonleung and Inleung. The tombs of Joseon's third king, Taejong (1367-1422), and his wife, Queen Wongyeong (1365-1420) are at Heonleung. Inleung is the resting place of Joseon's 23rd king, Sunjo (1790-1834), and his wife Queen Sunwon (1789-1857). Heonilleung is unique in that it houses two kings born 400 years apart. Visitors to the royal tombs can see examples of early and late Joseon Dynasty royal tombs and there is a weekly talk about the tombs every Saturday. On Lunar New Year's Day, traditional performances are held at Heonilleung for the public to enjoy.

_raw_content.post_desc: Cheong Wa Dae, meaning "Blue House," was the official residence of the President of South Korea until it was opened to the public in June 2022, becoming a popular tourist destination. The main building features the president's office, reception rooms, and conference rooms, while auxiliary buildings include Chunchugwan, the State Guest House, and the rear garden. Cheong Wa Dae is closed every Tuesday, and tour reservations can be made on its official website. A tour of the Cheong Wa Dae grounds, which encompasses Nokjiwon, Sangchunjae, the residence, the State Guest House, and the main building, typically takes around 1 hour and 30 minutes to 2 hours. On rainy days, interior tours of key buildings like the main building and Chunchugwan may be restricted to prevent damage. In the event of natural disasters such as typhoons, tours of all or parts of Cheong Wa Dae may be suspended to ensure visitor safety.

_raw_content.post_desc: 青瓦台”意为“蓝色瓦房”，曾是韩国总统官邸，但自2022年6月起向公众开放，成为一个旅游景点。主楼内设有总统办公室、接见室、会议室等，附属建筑包括春秋馆、迎宾馆、后苑等。青瓦台每周二休息，可通过青瓦台网站预约参观。 参观青瓦台的绿地园、常春斋、官邸、迎宾馆、主楼等整个园区，通常需要1小时30分到2小时。 在雨天，为了防止主楼、春秋馆等主要建筑内部损坏，可能会限制内部参观，在台风等自然灾害威胁游客安全的情况下，青瓦台区域的全部或部分参观可能会中止。

_raw_content.post_desc: The Institution of Natural Dyeing educates the public on traditional Korean dyeing methods. Though the main institute is based in the city of Bucheon in GyeongGi Province, visitors to Seoul can spend time at the institution's Seoul branch in Bukchon Hanok Village. Classes are held each week.

_raw_content.post_desc: The Jongienara Museum opened in 1999 as a Paper Art Museum and was established to revive and recreate Korea's world-class paper, K origami, and paper culture. Reopened as the Jongienara Museum in 2008, it goes beyond researching and introducing Korea's outstanding origami and paper culture. It pays attention to the excellent role of paper as a craft and art object, presenting the development of a new cultural art genre and modern paper culture and art. The excellence and creativity of Korean origami and paper culture are known to the public through the discovery, exhibitions, and education of current cultural paper artworks.

_raw_content.post_desc:
Cheongwadae Sarangchae is a historical memorial museum where visitors can learn about the past, present, and future visions of Seoul and Korea. Originally the home of the public information hall of Cheongwadae (the Blue House, the Korean presidential residence) called “Hyojadong Sarangbang”, it re-opened with its present name in January 2010 after extensive renovation. Cheongwadae Sarangchae is a two-story building, with exhibition halls, souvenir shops, a resting area on the first floor, and experience zones on the second floor.


Cheongwadae Sarangchae features the Korea Hall, the Hi Seoul Hall, a traditional handicrafts demonstration room, a souvenir shop, and a café on the first floor. Various cultural events, such as demonstrations of traditional handicrafts and traditional Korean tea tasting, are held regularly in the lobby. The souvenir shop stocks Cheongwadae-themed goods and traditional Korean items. After viewing the exhibitions, it is pleasant to take a break at the café and enjoy a cup of traditional Korean tea.


The Presidential Hall on the second floor displays material about the former presidents of Korea. Here visitors can explore the political and economic events of Korea from the past up to the present day via pictures and visuals. Visitors can also see at a glance a chronology of the past 60 years of Korean history, as well as the major events in the democratization and industrialization of Korea.

_raw_content.post_desc: Ssamziegil is a traditional culture and shopping complex in Insa-dong. Ssamziegil has over 70 shops including craft shops, galleries, tea houses, and restaurants. Located within the four-story complex is the Ssamziegil Experience Workshop, a place where visitors can learn how to make Korean arts & crafts first-hand. Visitors can learn how to design ceramic crafts like cups and dishes, make mother-of-pearl crafts like rings and cell phone accessories, and make hanji (Korean paper) crafts like jewel boxes and paper lamps. The workshop is located on the B1 level of Ssamziegil.

_raw_content.post_desc: Learn about the history of education in Korea at the Appenzeller Noble Memorial Museum. The museum is housed in what was once the Pai Chai Hakdang, which was Korea's first Western-style school. Currently, the school's classrooms have been repurposed and are used as a permanent exhibition hall, a special exhibition hall, an experience zone, and a seminar room. In the permanent exhibition hall, visitors can see what the Pai Chai Hakdang looked like in the 1930s at the hall's recreated historical classroom. Admission to the museum is free.

_raw_content.post_desc: The National Museum of Korean Contemporary History houses exhibitions that span modern Korean history, from the first opening of Korea to outsiders in the late 19th century to today. The museum is the country's first national museum of contemporary history. The eight-story museum has many facilities: there are four permanent exhibition halls and two special exhibition halls, seminar rooms, lecture halls, a rooftop garden, a museum shop (that sells souvenirs), a cafe, and storage lockers. The four permanent exhibitions cover different periods of Korean history and there are over 1,500 artifacts and items here. Some of the displays are patriot Ahn Jung-Geun's last writings, the March 1st Declaration of Independence, belongings of fallen soldiers from the Korean War, and materials relating to democratic activism. The museum's first floor contains two special exhibition halls. Here, you will find a variety of limited-time exhibitions relating to Korean history, politics, society, and culture. Additionally, visitors can listen to, watch, and experience the modernization of Korea through state-of-the-art technology. There is also the Children's Museum, where children can learn and experience history for themselves with the museum’s “Our History’s Treasure Chest” area.

_raw_content.post_desc:
韩国最早的国立近代历史博物馆“大韩民国历史博物馆”  

 

大韩民国历史博物馆于2012年12月26日正式开馆，这座承载了韩国历史的宝库记录了韩国从19世纪末期开放至如今的重大事件。 为了与国民共享文化，通过交流、调查、研究，资料收集设立了博物馆，向大家展示从苦难和逆境中不断发展的大韩民国的历史。 博物馆将韩国不同年代的历史通过4个展厅分别讲解说明。主要由第1展厅介绍“大韩民国的胎动”，第2展厅介绍“大韩民国基础的确立”，第3展厅介绍“大韩民国的成长与发展”，第4展厅介绍“大韩民国走向发达，迈向世界”等主题构成。 在“我们的历史宝库”儿童可以边体验边学习韩国的近代史。 另外，对整个近代史有多种主题的特别展示，通过展示来深度了解韩国近代史的内容于含义。 博物馆同时运营了多种教育项目与文化活动。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Upon opening its doors in 1978, the Kyunghee University Natural History Museum served as a little respite of nature in the city that boasted of a collection of nearly 90,000 specimen on display. The museum was initially founded upon the purpose of realizing the Kyungee University founding ideology of "Creating a world of culture" grounded in the results that had been obtained through several years of studying nature. The effort continues to approach the distancing relationship between nature and humankind amid rapid societal changes and urbanization with a "respite of nature in the city" that provides a sense of living in harmony with nature. 


All six floors of the museum display easy-to-understand exhibits capturing a comparison between the current state of evolution and the process of transformation up to the present-day with specimen of different plants and animals, as well as various rocks from sedimentary to igneous and metamorphic rocks that were used for research purposes by specialized teams of professors in various fields. There are courses and tour programs offered to help understand and practice nature preservation and the importance of life within the framework of these exhibited specimen. 


The Kyunghee University Natural History Museum has collected numerous specimen since the 1940s, while possessing a collection of more recent domestic specimen that have already become extinct or show signs of endangerment. The museum offers the opportunity for children and adults alike to more systematically learn about the classification and ecosystems of animals and plants and prioritizes itself with the fervor of exploring nature, as well as the awareness of nature protection.

_raw_content.post_desc:
キョンヒ(慶熙)大学自然史博物館は1978年に開館し、約9万点の標本(specimen)を所蔵している都心の中の小さな自然空間です。長年の自然研究に基づき、キョンヒ(慶熙)大学の創学精神である「文化世界創造」の実現のため開館しました。急速な社会変化と都市化により、自然から遠ざかっていく人々に、都心で共生する自然と生命を感じられる「都心の中の小さな自然空間」としてアプローチを試みています。


各分野の専門教授陣が研究用として収集した岩石(火成岩、堆積岩、変成岩)、化石、動植物標本を、生物の進化とこれまでの生態変化をわかりやすく理解できるよう、6つのフロアで展示しており、この展示標本を基に自然保存と生命の重要性を理解し、実践できるよう教育と観覧案内を行っています。


自然史博物館に保存されている標本は、生命工学技術を活用して私たちが有効に利用できる産物を創出できるため、後世に伝えるべき大切な資源です。キョンヒ(慶熙)大学自然史博物館は1940年代から標本を収集しており、韓国ですでに絶滅したり、最近姿を消した絶滅危惧種も所蔵しています。


キョンヒ(慶熙)大学自然史博物館は、子供から大人までの動植物の分類と生態を体系的に学習し、自然探求の意欲と自然保護意識を伝えることを重要視しています。

_raw_content.post_desc:
庆熙大学自然史博物馆建于1978年，是收藏了约9万多件标本的市中心小自然空间。以长期研究自然的结果为基础，为实现庆熙大学创学精神“文化世界创造”做出努力。对于因社会快速变化与城市化而与自然渐行渐远的他们来说，为了能够感受到在城市中一起生活的自然和生命，一直致力于努力向“城市中的小自然空间”靠近。

为了让各领域专门教授团队能够轻松理解生物进化现状及其间的生态变化，博物馆内收藏了庆熙大学各学科领域专业教授用于研究而采集的岩石、化石、动植物等标本，共分6层，以进行教育和参观，以便理解和实践自然保护和生命的重要性。

自然史博物馆保存的标本是利用生命工学技术，可以创造出韩国人可以使用的产物。庆熙大学自然史博物馆从20世纪40年代开始收集标本，还收藏有在韩国已灭绝或最近销声匿迹的濒危物种。

庆熙大学自然史博物馆从儿童到成人，系统地学习动植物的分类和生态，重视传达自然探索的欲望和自然保护意识。

extra.cmmn_important:
Seafood Shopping Tips:
The Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market has a lot of price fluctuations because the amount of seafood that comes in every day is different. To cope with these market characteristics and purchase at a lower price, refer to the market price for each type of fish provided on the Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market's website (http://www.susansijang.co.kr). It tells you the quantity and market price of seafood by fish type every day, so if you refer to it in advance, you can know the approximate price trend.

_raw_content.post_desc: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market (or Noryangjin Fish Market for short) is the best place in Seoul to get fresh seafood at competitive prices. The market is both a wholesale outlet, trading in daily catches that arrive from every possible location, and also a retail market, where the public can get seafood at very low prices. The market is easily reached since it is conveniently connected to the subway station. The market is the largest fish market in Seoul. There are many restaurants ready to slice any fish bought at the market into hoe (raw fish) for their customers. During lunch and supper times, the market is bustling with customers browsing for fresh seafood. Nearby restaurants are ready to slice the fish that customers buy directly from the market into hoe. The usual arrangement is that the customer pays the fishmonger for the fish and the restaurant owner for the side dishes, vegetables or sauces. Daily auctions also take place from 1 am to 4 am. Among merchants, competition is fierce to get the freshest seafood, and tourists as well as citizens of Seoul like to come down to see this unusual scene. It is great fun to see and taste a wide range of seafood at the market, and everything bought and sold here comes fresh from the ocean.

_raw_content.post_desc: ノリャンジン(鷺梁津)水産市場はソウルで最も大きい水産物市場、ついさっき海から水揚げされたような生きた魚介類が所狭しと並んでいます。地下鉄と連結しているのでアクセスしやすく、市民や観光客が手軽に利用できます。競りは、貝類が深夜1時、鮮魚は1時30分、活魚は3時に始まります。刺身料理店も軒を連ねていて、新鮮な魚介類をその場で調理してもらい食べることもできます。刺身の代金は魚を選んだ後市場で支払い、野菜や調味料代は食堂で支払うという方式です。春には主にタイやスズキを求めるお客が多く、真夏にはウナギの蒲焼きやタラバガニが、秋には焼きヒラが有名です。冬は刺身が人気ですが、特にカキを味わいに多くの人がやって来ます。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market is famous for its “dokkaebi sale” held three times a week. The market sells various agricultural and marine products, including fruits and vegetables at low prices, attracting many shoppers. In particular, the market offers great value bargains in sales leading up to New Year's Day and Chuseok (Korean harvest festival). The market has 87 stores and 13 street vendors equipped with modern facilities, making it a convenient place to browse.  The origin of the market dates back to 1982 when unlicensed street vendors began gathering here one by one, selling their goods in the evenings to avoid police patrols. Whenever officers came to the market to crack down, the vendors would disappear in an instant, earning the nickname, “dokkaebi”. Dokkaebi is a mythical being that appears in many old Korean folktales and is similar to a hobgoblin. During the early 2000s, the market faced crisis and risk of closure when a number of major discount supermarkets opened. In spite of this, since the market was renovated in 2004 it has grown to become one of the busiest traditional markets. 


Many items in Banghak-dong Dokkaebi Market are priced 30 to 40 percent cheaper than in the major supermarkets. In the middle of the market, displays of the most popular items can be found in every shop at 20 to 30 percent cheaper. The market also holds huge bargain sales before the festive seasons.  Traditional Korean banchan (side dishes) can be purchased at very reasonable prices in Banchan stores. It is very common to see overseas visitors in the market buying different types of banchan. These include Kimchi and Tteok, traditional Korean cakes. The market also has sections for fruit and vegetables, seafood and meat. Cosmetics and confectionery are also sold in the market at cheap prices. Seafood and meat are delivered directly from their place of origin, so customers can be sure they are buying fresh produce.

_raw_content.post_desc:
Dongmyo Flea Market started life in the late 1980s. Every day an array of street stalls open up along the stone walls of Dongmyo Park. The main items bought and sold here are antiques of every type, including items such as wallets, electronics, old books, film posters etc. Recently vintage clothing and shoes have become the main area of interest. Prices are typically around 1,000 won so you can have fun browsing and shopping without worrying about the cost. 


There are all kinds of items from everyday miscellaneous goods to antiques. If you get peckish while shopping, boiled duck's eggs cost just 1,500 won each or bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) make very satisfying snacks. The market is always crowded with people at weekends. The most popular item in Dongmyo Flea Market is used clothing. When new stocks arrive, the market is packed with people looking for bargains. Prices are normally around 1,000 won, but leather items or furs reach around 10,000 won. Designer labels can reach over 100,000 won. The best time for shopping is on weekend afternoons.

_raw_content.post_desc: スンインドン(崇仁洞)蚤の市では、トンミョ(東廟)公園の石垣沿いに毎日露天が広げられ、衣類、靴、財布から時計や電子製品、古書、映画ポスターに至るまであらゆる骨董品が取り引きされます。最近はビンテージ服が主流です。ショッピングをして小腹が空けばアヒルのゆで卵やピンデットクなどでお腹を満たすことができます。ここは、週末にはいつも多くの市民で混み合っています。毎週金曜の夕方、「井戸端競り」が開かれます。「クチョンダン(旧天堂)漢医院」の3階で、ここでは近現代100年の歴史が詰まった資料や生活遺物の競売が行われています。前大臣からチョンゲチョン(清渓川)の露天商まで参加者の顔ぶれは非常に多彩です。競売はふつうKRW1,000から始まります。(問い合わせ：+82-2-2254-4613)近所に宝物142号「トンミョ(東廟)公園」があります。入場料は無料で、スンインドン(崇仁洞)蚤の市を観光したあと一緒に見て回るのもよいでしょう。

_raw_content.post_desc: Songwoldong is a neighborhood in northern Seoul that is home to many of the city's historic sites. Deoksugung Palace, the Seoul Museum of History, Gyeonghuigung Palace, Sungnyemun Gate, Seodaemun Prison History Hall and Dongnimmun Gate are all found in Songwoldong. Visitors to Seoul can experience Korean history through a visit to this beautiful and charming area. The area has also been used as a filming location for many Korean TV shows including "Rooftop Prince." Songwoldong is easily accessible by car or public transportation.

_raw_content.post_desc: 1898 Myeongdong Cathedral is a complex cultural space frequented by many people and was built as a place that would facilitate communication and sharing. Built in 1898, tt was the first Gothic style building ever constructed in Korea and the first to be built with red brick. Reminiscent of the way beams of sun shine down, the interior ceilings are angled and this makes for a warm and cozy effect on the entire space. Visitors may also shop for flowers and souvenirs, and even enjoy some of the unique classes that are offered to help take in some fascinating culture, books, music. and more.

_raw_content.post_desc:
心の通じ合いと分かち合いを実践する複合文化空間
「1898 myeongdong cathedral(明洞大聖堂)」は、多くの人とのコミュニケーションの実践のために作られた複合文化空間である。 1898年、ジョンヒョン(鐘峴)の丘に赤レンガで初めて作られたミョンドン・ソンダン(明洞聖堂)の建築的ゴシック様式を受け継ぎ、現代的に再解釈して建てられた複合文化空間だ。

立体的に表現された天井より差し込む居心地の良い日差しが暖かい空間を作り、多くの人々のための憩いの場所となっている。カフェでは談話を交わしたり、本や音楽と映像もリラックスして楽しめる優しい空間となっている。

_raw_content.post_desc:
ヨイド(汝矣島)に位置している韓国公営放送KBSは本館と新館、KBSホール、KBSオン等の施設が備わっています。KBS見学ホール、KBSオン(KBS・Tourhall)は韓国放送の歴史と現在を体験出来る放送展示館です。先端映像マルチタッチモニターを通じてジャンル別、時代別にドラマと芸能番組の映像を鑑賞出来るメディア体験館やなどを観覧する事ができます。また9時のニュースアンカー体験館、仮想スタジオなどで放送製作現場を体験してみる事も出来て異色体験を求める観光客にオススメのスポット。実際生放送で伝われるラジオプログラムを見たり聞いたりする事が出来るラジオオープンスタジオも備わっています。1,900席の座席と最先端舞台装置、ミキシング、照明施設を揃えたKBSホールと新館で広がる音楽放送を通じてファンとスターの出会いや疎通の場となっています。

韓流スター俳優キム・スヒョンが出演したドラマ「プロデューサー」の背景になったヨイド(汝矣島)KBSは韓流ファンの必須観光コースとして愛されています。得にラジオ生放送の現場を直接観覧しスターと近くで疎通できるラジオ・オープンスタジオとKBSホールや新館で広がる音楽放送を通じて直接スターに出会い、最新K-POPの公演も観覧する事ができます。

_raw_content.post_desc:
男女老少都可以在手办博物馆W享受乐趣和与众不同的游戏。这是一家以手办和玩具为素材的主题公园式博物馆，可理解和获得关于手办的信息，并亲身体验、实现心灵的交流。从无敌铁金刚Z、GUNDAM、Robot  Taekwon V等著名手办展览到超人、蝙蝠侠、钢铁侠等耳熟能详的英雄手办、高价的限量版手办，各种手办以尖端展示形式展出。可通过咨询手办专家购买产品。地下咖啡厅、体验区、游乐区、拍照区中还能留下美好回忆。也可参与以幼儿及小学生团体、青少年和普通人为对象的“手办制作”教育项目。

成人孩童化文化是指“带有儿童性情和趣向的成人”，在韩国也作为一种文化而迅速成长并获得了一定地位。手办博物馆W起着这样一种作用。因EXO的DO、演员李钟硕、李光洙、高小英、林时完等喜欢手办的韩流明星们常来访此处而更加炙手可热。也是电视剧《Oh My Venus》中韩流明星苏志燮和申敏儿浪漫的约会场景拍摄地。

_raw_content.post_desc:
Gwanghwamun Square is located on Sejong-ro in Jongno-gu and is vast in size. Gwanghwamun Square stretches out from Gwanghwamun Gate, towards Cheonggyecheon Stream, and is divided into 6 sections: “Recovering the History of Gwanghwamun Gate Plaza,” “Reenacting Yukjo Street Plaza,” “Korea Main Plaza,” “Civil Participation Urban Culture Plaza,” “Downtown Plaza” and “Cheonggyecheon Stream Connector.”  

 

The focal point of the square is the statue of King Sejong the Great. During the day, the square is always busy with people but at night it is a tranquil and beautiful tourist attraction. Gwanghwamun Square, with Inwangsan Mountain just behind it, is not just a beautiful tourist locale. The square has over 600 years of history and it is a place where the spirit of the Korean nation can be felt.

_raw_content.post_desc:
就像中国的剪纸工艺一样，韩国也有用传统纸张做载体的韩纸工艺流传至今。中国女性在剪纸艺术的发展上做出了重要的贡献，韩纸工艺也是韩国的闺房女子们在使用韩纸制作日常用品的过程中发展起来的。在这个工坊展示着各种用韩纸制作的服装、饰品、画作、屏风和各种家具，令人目不暇接。

剪纸是用剪刀将纸剪成各种形状的镂空艺术，而韩纸工艺则主要将韩纸层层糊起，制成立体的用具，或者用纸糊、纸绳等制成各种器皿。在这个工坊，您可以亲自动手制作些小物件，体会一下韩纸工艺的魅力。
